RFC9012-13-10.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: an unrecognized sub-TLV changing how the TLV is processed. The units assert on TunnelTLV.Preference, whose only non-test caller is internal/test/decode (the test display decoder): no product path processes any sub-TLV, so the assertion proves a reader Ze never uses. What Ze does with the TLV (parse and carry) is covered by 13-11.

RFC9012-13-11.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: dropping an unrecognized sub-TLV when the route is propagated. TestRFC9012AllSubTLVsPropagate proves ParseTunnelEncap then WriteTo keeps both sub-TLVs, not the route distribution path; the negative compares against an attribute the test built without them, which exercises no Ze behaviour. No {single-polarity} marker.

RFC9012-13-12.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: a malformed sub-TLV handled other than as unrecognized. The units assert that TunnelTLV.Preference skips a wrong-length Preference; Preference's only non-test caller is internal/test/decode (the test display decoder), so no product path processes the sub-TLV and the assertion proves a reader Ze never uses. The carry half (still enumerated and round-tripped) is ParseTunnelEncap then WriteTo, not the distribution path.

RFC9012-13-16.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: acting on a sub-TLV meaningless for the tunnel type. The units assert TunnelTLV.Preference is unchanged by a VXLAN Encapsulation sub-TLV in a type-15 TLV; Preference's only non-test caller is internal/test/decode (the test display decoder), so no product path processes sub-TLVs and the assertion proves a reader Ze never uses.

RFC9012-13-18.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: calling a TLV with a meaningless sub-TLV malformed. The positive enforces it: the attribute holding a VXLAN Encapsulation sub-TLV in a type-15 TLV parses and both sub-TLVs enumerate. The negative (truncated TLV header refused) is a framing rule, a neighbouring one, and the row carries no {single-polarity} marker.

RFC9012-13-19.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Clauses: the meaningless sub-TLV is not malformed, and is not removed before distribution. The positive is ParseTunnelEncap then WriteTo on test-built bytes, not the route distribution path. The negative compares two byte strings the test built (with and without the sub-TLV), which exercises no Ze behaviour. No {single-polarity} marker.

RFC9012-13-3.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: calling an attribute with an unrecognized tunnel type malformed. The positive enforces it: TestRFC9012UnrecognizedTunnelTypeIsCarried fails if ParseTunnelEncap (the registered attribute parser, wire.go knownAttrParsers) refuses the 0xFFFE TLV. The negative (TLV length overrun refused) is the framing rule of 13-1/13-2, a neighbouring rule, and the row carries no {single-polarity} marker.

RFC9012-13-5.note: SB-3 strict re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: dropping the unrecognized TLV when the route is propagated. The positive is ParseTunnelEncap then WriteTo on test-built bytes, not the route distribution path. The negative (TestRFC9012UnrecognizedTLVRemovalIsObservable) compares two byte strings the test built, which exercises no Ze behaviour. No {single-polarity} marker.

RFC9012-13-7.note: the RFC sentence covers the seven RFC 9012 single-instance sub-TLVs (Tunnel Egress Endpoint, Encapsulation, DS, UDP Destination Port, Embedded Label Handling, MPLS Label Stack, Prefix-SID); TestRFC9012DuplicateSingleInstanceSubTLVs duplicates the RFC 9830 Preference sub-TLV (type 12), which is not in that list, and ze decodes none of the seven (TunnelTLV.Preference in internal/core/bgp/attribute/tunnel_encap.go is the only sub-TLV reader). The assertions are correct evidence for RFC9830-2.4-1, which the same lines also tag, not for this row

RFC9012-13-8.note: positive duplicates the RFC 9830 Preference sub-TLV, not one of the RFC 9012 single-instance types the sentence names; ParseTunnelEncap and SubTLVs are type-blind so the behavior likely holds, but no buffer with a duplicated listed type (e.g. two Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLVs) is asserted. The negative (stray trailing octet refused) violates the TLV framing rule, not this one

RFC9012-13-9.note: the sentence is the duplicate-sub-TLV paragraph's propagation clause; TestRFC9012AllSubTLVsPropagate round-trips one Preference and two unknown sub-TLVs with no duplicate, so an implementation that dropped second occurrences on propagation would pass this unit (duplicate round-trip is asserted only in the 13-8/13-7 unit, with a non-listed type)
